rationale: The original context in O'Kelly et al. directly supports the claim. The paper explicitly contrasts rare-event simulation against requiring hundreds of millions or billions of test miles, and formally defines its risk-based framework as estimating the probability of a dangerous event p_gamma := P0(f(X) <= gamma) conditional on a base distribution P0 modeling traffic behavior, a physics-based/perceptual simulator, and a chosen threshold gamma. All inspected artifact uses preserve this conditional boundary and do not treat the research study as regulatory approval or unconditional proof of safety.
evidence_locators: PDF p. 2, Section 1 (base distribution P0, simulator realization X, and threshold gamma in Eq. 1)
limitations: Inspection is limited to the provided preprint text (arXiv:1811.00145v3); it does not validate simulator fidelity, empirical convergence of the estimator, or transferability beyond the evaluated highway scenario.
